findings.evidence: Lines 242-245 and 256-259: `def covarianceForm (c c' : ι → ℝ) : ℝ := c ⬝ᵥ D.covariance *ᵥ c'` and `def variance (c : ι → ℝ) : ℝ := D.covarianceForm c c` — neither mentions `D.value`, while `IsNoiseModel.variance_dotProduct` (line 349) is the statement that makes the random reading true.
findings.fix: Describe them as the covariance/variance of the measured value of the functional `c`, i.e. of `c ⬝ᵥ X` for any noise model, pointing at `IsNoiseModel.covariance_dotProduct` / `IsNoiseModel.variance_dotProduct`; drop `c ⬝ᵥ value` from both docstrings.
findings.issue: `covarianceForm` is documented as "the covariance of the linear functionals `c ⬝ᵥ value` and `c' ⬝ᵥ value`" and `variance` (line 256) as "the variance of the linear functional `c ⬝ᵥ value`". `value : ι → ℝ` is the central-value vector, so `c ⬝ᵥ value` is a fixed real number whose variance and covariance are zero; the quantity actually described is the (co)variance of `c ⬝ᵥ X` under a noise model, and neither definition depends on `value` at all.

findings.evidence: Structure field at line 195: `integral_eq_value : ∀ i, μ[X i] = D.value i`.
findings.fix: Replace "the noise" with "the random data `X`" (or "the noise model `X`") in all four docstrings; reserve "noise" for the fluctuation `X - value` if it is ever introduced.
findings.issue: Four `IsNoiseModel` lemma docstrings call `c ⬝ᵥ X` "a linear combination of the noise": lines 333-334, 341-342, 347-348 and 354-356. `X` is not noise — `IsNoiseModel.integral_eq_value` fixes `μ[X i] = D.value i`, so `X` is the random realisation of the data and its mean is the central values, not zero. The phrasing contradicts the very lemma stated at line 335 ("the mean of a linear combination of the noise is the corresponding functional of the central values").

summary: Module docstrings and declaration docs are present, accurate in their Mathlib citations, and free of process narrative. Two docstring groups misdescribe their objects: the variance/covariance forms are documented as the (co)variance of deterministic numbers, and four noise-model lemmas call the random data `X` "the noise" although its mean is the central values.
